# ethereum-optimism/specs Weekly Report (Jun 14 - 20, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s activity centered on refining the protocol's Zero-Knowledge (ZK) infrastructure and clarifying execution specifications for the Lagoon SDM. A significant portion of the work involved transitioning ZK-related implementation tasks, such as bond claiming and CI proofing strategies, to external repositories for specialized tracking. These efforts ensure that the protocol specifications remain lean while providing clear guidance for the ongoing integration of ZK components into the OP Stack.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol Specification Refinements
The team focused on technical precision within the Lagoon SDM specification to ensure consistent execution behavior across the network.
*   **Lagoon SDM Warming Clarification:** A critical update was made to the Lagoon SDM specification regarding block-level warming. The clarification specifies that block-level warming excludes intrinsically-warm accesses. This ensures that only state accesses charged the EIP-2929 "cold" price are eligible for rebates, maintaining the economic integrity of the gas model ([#919](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/919)).

### ZK Infrastructure & Execution
Discussions continued regarding the technical requirements for supporting ZK execution within the protocol's tooling.
*   **VM-Runner ZK Support:** Technical scoping for `vm-runner` indicates that ZK execution will likely require a Rust-based implementation due to dependencies on `sp1`. Current proposals include embedding a Rust executor within a Docker image or adding a specific option to `vm-runner` to drive the executor while minimizing new code by leveraging existing proposer components ([#18325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18325)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
Several issues were closed this week as the project moved from specification/decision phases to active implementation in other repositories:
*   **ZKDisputeGame Bond Management:** Issues regarding how to handle bond credits assigned to `address(0)` were closed. The team decided that while leaving bonds in `delayedweth` (effectively soft-burning them) was a possibility, a formal fix—either via `dispute-mon` auto-claiming or a contract change—will be tracked in a separate repository ([#19743](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19743), [#21420](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21420)).
*   **CI/Local Proofing Strategy:** The project finalized the strategy for ZK proofs in development environments. To manage costs and efficiency, a mock prover will be used for CI and local development. Future considerations include using `op-sepolia` for periodic production-grade proving once the necessary infrastructure is available ([#21409](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21409)).

### Active Issues
*   **ZK Execution Dependencies:** The primary active technical hurdle remains the integration of Rust-based ZK execution into the existing Go-heavy infrastructure, specifically within the `vm-runner` utility ([#18325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18325)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by high-level architectural decision-making, particularly regarding the ZK roadmap. Collaboration focused on determining the boundaries between the protocol specifications and the practical implementation of ZK components. The decision to move several tracking issues to external repositories suggests a shift toward active development and integration testing within the broader Optimism ecosystem. Discussions around bond claiming and CI strategies showed a pragmatic approach to protocol security, balancing the need for "honest challenger" incentives with the technical overhead of managing edge-case bond distributions.
